critical_code_review_comments: OPTIONAL P2 (unchanged from iter-45) · engine.on_trade_closed still fires a background self._persist_risk (line ~841) while apply_broker_deal awaits persist_risk_now moments later. Two writes to the same doc via two code paths is still racy in practice — the iter-45 fix correctly handles the race, but suppressing the redundant bg write when the sync path is imminent (or short-circuiting on the sync callsite) would eliminate the race entirely and drop one Mongo round-trip per close. Not blocking.

OPTIONAL P3 (unchanged) · bridge_routes.poll_trades $max on max_order_epoch happens BEFORE the readback — intentional read-after-write semantic; a one-line comment near line ~562 would improve readability.
OPTIONAL P4 (unchanged) · poll_trades response body could echo the epoch used for the dispatch decision to make EA-side forensics easier if a legitimate scalp trade is ever fence-cancelled.

OPTIONAL P5 (unchanged) · audit_backlog surfaces service_block, but there is no admin API to clear it once the offending unique index has been dropped out-of-band. A `set_service_block(None)` admin route would ease ops recovery.

New OBSERVATION · The fix path in persist_risk_now performs update_one → find_one → (if equal/older) another update_one, then always calls _fenced_account_write which repeats the same pattern for _ACCOUNT. In the worst case this is 4 write RPCs + 2 read RPCs per close event. Acceptable given the correctness guarantee, but could be collapsed to a single upsert-with-fence via aggregation-pipeline $set if latency matters later.

rca of the issue: iter-45 RCA was correct and the fix in engine.py addresses it precisely: the fence-rejection path in persist_risk_now/_fenced_account_write now checks that the observed existing doc's lease_epoch is STRICTLY GREATER than the runner's epoch before raising 'fenced out'. When the epoch is equal (the self-race against the worker's own bg _persist_risk between update_one and find_one) or older (should never happen with proper leasing, defensive), the code performs a retry of the fenced $set — which succeeds because the doc now exists. Verified end-to-end (external-deal close → applied ledger + complete broker_deals) and unit-level (strictly-newer epoch still raises for both per-symbol and _ACCOUNT branches). No open issues.
